item.title: Church not a political party — Bishop Mike Okonkwo
item.description: By Olayinka Latona The Fountain of Life Church today held its Sunday service despite reports of a court injunction against Pastor Jimmy Odukoya. Addressing the crowded congregation, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya said he had not received any court injunction as reported, and stressed his unwavering love for the church. Members were said to have chanted “We love you” during the service. Bishop Mike Okonkwo of The Redeemed Evangelical Ministry, one of the spiritual fathers to the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, ministered on the theme “The Glory of The Church.” He charged members and ministers of the church to diligently keep the founder’s legacy and remain steadfast in Christ, reminding them of the advice he gave when the church founder died. “The responsibility fell on us to talk to… The only honour we can do for the sacrifice, the process, pains and everything that the man of God who is highly celebrated in this country is that his legacy must continue,” Bishop Okonkwo said. “And I told you that day that Fountain will never die. No matter the trial or temptation, this is a work that is solidly laid. The price has been paid; lives have been lost. There is no power of hell that would destroy this work. It will go from glory to glory.” Acknowledging recent online attacks, he said: “For the past one or two weeks, we have been literally battered on social media. There is nothing that has not been said, both what is true and what is not true. Phone calls from far and near: ‘Bishop Mike, where are you?’ You can’t separate me from Fountain; it’s not possible, because it’s a covenant established by God Himself. What affects Fountain affects me. Don’t think that I am just aloof. I said to myself, ‘God, you just have to give us wisdom.’” He added: “The day you fully understand the glory of God upon His church and what it takes to give birth to His church, then there is nothing from the gates of hell that will move you.” Bishop Okonkwo warned that the church is not a political party but God’s house. “The church is not a human institution; it’s God’s house; it belongs to Him. Think of the price that He paid for the church. We should all know that we are not for Tolu, Jimmy or the Board of Trustees; none of them died for you,” he said. “The church is not a political party because Jesus Christ’s life was involved. The church is not an ordinary thing. We must be careful that none of us is an instrument to destroy the church of Christ.” He declared that God is interested in the church and that its best days are ahead. “God is interested in this church, in case you don’t know. What you have seen so far cannot be compared to what is coming, because everything that has to do with God is always progressive. item.title: ABUAD warns students against cultism, cybercrime
item.description: Varsity matriculates 2,442 students for 2026/2027 session By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI — Afe Babalola University, Ado-Ekiti (ABUAD), has warned newly admitted students against cultism, cybercrime, substance abuse and other social vices capable of undermining their education and future. The university also cautioned the students against examination malpractice, bullying and the irresponsible use of artificial intelligence, urging them to uphold discipline, integrity and academic excellence. The Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Smaranda Olarinde, gave the warning at the institution’s 18th matriculation ceremony held over the weekend, where 2,442 students were formally admitted for the 2026/2027 academic session. The figure comprises 2,089 regular undergraduate students, 77 Open and Distance Learning students and 276 part-time students. Giving a breakdown of the undergraduate admissions, Olarinde said 306 students were admitted into the College of Social and Management Sciences, 307 into Sciences, 275 into Pharmacy, 684 into Medicine and Health Sciences, 171 into Law and 346 into Engineering. Addressing the students, the vice-chancellor described their admission as an opportunity that required discipline, responsibility and commitment to academic excellence. She urged them to be mindful of their associations, noting that their choice of friends could influence their habits, reputation, academic performance and future. According to her, university education goes beyond obtaining certificates to include character formation, emotional maturity, leadership development and the acquisition of values needed to contribute meaningfully to society. Olarinde urged the students to uphold the university’s philosophy of Labour, Service and Integrity, stressing that hard work, selfless service and honesty should guide their academic and professional pursuits. She also cautioned against the misuse of artificial intelligence and other emerging digital technologies, warning students not to present machine-generated materials or another person’s intellectual work as their original research. “The company you keep will influence your habits, attitude, reputation and ultimately your destiny. Surround yourselves with people who encourage learning, discipline, honesty and constructive ambition. “Stay away from cultism, substance abuse, bullying, examination malpractice, cybercrime and every other form of misconduct that can destroy your future and bring disrepute to your family and this university. “No momentary pleasure or misguided friendship is worth the sacrifice of your education, character or good name,” she said. On the use of artificial intelligence, the vice-chancellor said the technology could support research, improve productivity and create new opportunities for learning, but should not replace independent thinking, genuine scholarship or personal integrity. “Use digital tools responsibly. item.title: NELFUND considers increase in N20,000 monthly student upkeep
item.description: By Joseph Erunke Millions of Nigerian students benefiting from the Federal Government’s student loan scheme may soon receive higher monthly upkeep allowances as the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, NELFUND, considers a review of the current N20,000 payment amid mounting pressure from rising living costs. The possibility of an increase emerged as NELFUND acknowledged that the existing allowance might require adjustment to better reflect the financial realities facing students struggling to meet the costs of feeding, transportation, accommodation and other basic necessities while pursuing their education. The fund’s Managing Director, Akintunde Sawyer, disclosed this during an interview on Beyond the Headlines,a TVC news programme, where he said the monthly upkeep payment was under constant review. Although he did not announce a new figure or a timeline for implementation, Sawyer signalled that an adjustment was being considered, raising expectations among students who have repeatedly complained that the current ₦20,000 monthly allowance is inadequate to survive on in the face of escalating prices. “Are we considering it? Yes, of course. It’s under constant review,” he said. The indication of a possible increase comes against the backdrop of growing concerns over the purchasing power of students, many of whom depend on the NELFUND intervention to cushion the financial burden of higher education. With food prices, transportation fares, accommodation costs and other essential expenses continuing to weigh heavily on households, the N20,000 monthly upkeep has increasingly come under scrutiny over its capacity to provide meaningful relief to beneficiaries. However, Sawyer said any decision to increase the allowance would have to be carefully weighed against the fund’s financial capacity and the need to sustain support for the growing number of students enrolled in the scheme. He explained that while NELFUND was conscious of the need to improve students’ welfare, it could not make adjustments without considering the implications for the entire beneficiary population. “What we need to do is plan it in such a way that it doesn’t put us in a situation where we can’t cater for the totality of the people that we need to cater for,” Sawyer said. Beyond the proposed review by NELFUND, Sawyer disclosed that President Bola Tinubu was also considering an intervention aimed at providing students with more meaningful financial support to enable them to remain in school and successfully complete their academic programmes. Although he did not disclose the nature, scope or financial details of the proposed presidential intervention, the NELFUND chief suggested that the government was exploring ways to improve the level of assistance available to students. “I know the President certainly is looking at intervening in a way that helps the students have more meaningful sustenance so that they can get through their courses,” he said. item.title: Nigerian sentenced to 24 months in US prison over COVID-19 relief fraud
item.description: A Nigerian man, Chukwuebuka Arinze, has been sentenced to two years in prison in the United States for using another person’s identity to fraudulently apply for COVID-19 relief funds. Arinze, 38, was convicted of aggravated identity theft after using a farmer’s Social Security number to submit an application under the US government’s Coronavirus Food Assistance Program. He was sentenced on October 30, 2026, by US District Judge Robert Rossiter Jr. at a federal court in Omaha, Nebraska, according to the US Attorney’s Office for the District of Nebraska. The Nigerian will also serve one year of supervised release after his imprisonment and face deportation from the United States, the statement said. Prosecutors said Arinze, who was living outside the US at the time, sent an email to the Farm Service Agency office in Wayne, Nebraska, on September 28, 2020, seeking financial assistance under the programme. The email, titled “CFAP Forms,” contained an application for the second phase of the Coronavirus Food Assistance Program, known as CFAP2, alongside an Automated Clearing House payment form. Both documents were submitted in the name of a dairy farmer identified in court records as Victim 1 and contained the farmer’s Social Security number. The US authorities said Arinze knowingly used the identification number belonging to the farmer without authorisation to validate the application. He was later brought to the United States to face prosecution over the offence. The Coronavirus Food Assistance Program was established by the US Department of Agriculture during the COVID-19 pandemic to support agricultural producers affected by declining sales and rising marketing costs. The initiative was administered through the department’s Farm Service Agency and Agricultural Marketing Service. Its first phase ran from May 26 to September 11, 2020, while the second phase, CFAP2, opened from September 21 to December 11 of the same year. The programme allowed applicants to self-certify their eligibility without submitting evidence of pandemic-related business losses. The Federal Bureau of Investigation investigated the case. item.title: Ogun PDP deputy guber candidate installed Akinkanju of Egbaland
item.description: By Jimoh Babatunde The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) Deputy Governorship Candidate in Ogun State for the 2027 election, Hajia Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, has been installed as the first Akinkanju of Egbaland by the Alake and Paramount Ruler of Egbaland, Oba Adedotun Aremu Gbadebo, Okukenu IV. The installation took place at the Alake Palace on Saturday as part of activities marking the monarch’s 21st coronation anniversary. Sowunmi-Kolapo, who was previously honoured with the title of Iyalode of Ijemo, is also the Iya Sunnah of Egbaland and Ameerah of Ogun State. According to the palace, the new title, the first of its kind, was conferred on her in recognition of her contributions to the development of Egbaland and her commitment to the community. Oba Gbadebo urged her to remain committed to service, cultural preservation and the promotion of unity across Egbaland. The ceremony attracted prominent personalities, including government officials, business leaders, traditional rulers and politicians. The Ogun State PDP governorship candidate, Oladipupo Adebutu, led other party leaders to celebrate with his running mate. Speaking at the reception held at the Abeokuta Sports Club, Sowunmi-Kolapo expressed gratitude for the honour, particularly acknowledging the Alake for the recognition. She also described the conferment as significant ahead of the 2027 governorship election, saying the people of Ogun State had spoken through the honour. The deputy governorship candidate maintained that the forthcoming election should transcend party affiliations, insisting that the people must resist any alleged attempt to undermine the state’s interests. “We are indigenes of Ogun State. We do not run from battles. It is in our DNA to always resist intimidation and protect our independence. “I’m humbled by this gracious conferment of the title of the 1st Akinkanju of Egbaland on me by His Royal Majesty. “I pray to justify the confidence reposed in me by our traditional rulers, our respected elders, who have continued to stand for our heritage, the people of Egbaland, and the people of Ogun State in general. “Our father, the Alake of Egbaland, has spoken. Let us work hard to continue to have an Egba community that is first among others,” she said. Also honoured at the ceremony was Senator Iyabo Obasanjo, who was installed as the first Iyaniwura of Egbaland by the Alake. In his remarks, Adebutu congratulated his running mate and the other honourees, describing their recognition as well deserved. He said Sowunmi-Kolapo’s elevation from Iyalode of Ijemo to Akinkanju of Egbaland reflected her years of service, loyalty, courage, motherly leadership and commitment to the unity and development of the Egba people. Adebutu also congratulated Obasanjo on her installation as the first Iyaniwura of Egbaland, describing the honour as recognition of her distinguished public service and contributions to Egbaland and Nigeria. item.title: NDLEA arrests South African golfer, Kenyan chef over drug trafficking
item.description: Agency intercepts 160 explosives bound for Zamfara, seizes 4.6 tonnes of cannabis in Osun By Kingsley Omonobi The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has arrested a 37-year-old South African professional golfer, Grobler Henlo, and a 25-year-old Kenyan chef, Abubakar Faiza Njambi, over an alleged attempt to smuggle 50.40 kilogrammes of Loud, a potent strain of cannabis, into Nigeria. The suspects were arrested at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA), Ikeja, Lagos, following the interception of the illicit consignment. The NDLEA spokesman, Femi Babafemi, said the golfer’s arrest came exactly one month before the agency intercepted an American professional basketball player, Greene Da’monte Khiree, at the same airport on November 11, 2026, over the importation of 33.95 kilogrammes of the same psychoactive substance. According to the agency, Henlo arrived in Lagos from South Africa aboard a South African Airways flight on October 11 and was intercepted at the Terminal 2 arrival hall. A search of two travelling boxes in his possession reportedly led to the discovery of 46 parcels of Loud weighing 50.40 kilogrammes. Investigations revealed that although the boxes were in Henlo’s possession, they bore the luggage tags of his alleged accomplice, Njambi, who had collected two other boxes bearing his tags from the airport conveyor belt before leaving the airport. The agency said the exchange of luggage tags was a deliberate attempt by the syndicate to frustrate the identification of ownership and enable each courier to deny the boxes bearing their respective names if intercepted. During preliminary questioning, Henlo reportedly disclosed that he was recruited by a South African associate identified as Shanel, who linked him with other members of the syndicate whom he had never met physically. He said a driver picked him up from his home in South Africa, handed him four travelling boxes and took him to the airport, where he was instructed to meet Njambi and exchange luggage tags. The golfer reportedly said he was promised 5,000 South African rand upon successful delivery of the consignment. Further examination revealed that tracking devices had been installed in the travelling boxes and on his mobile phone, a development the agency said was similar to what was discovered in the bags abandoned by the American basketball player a month later. The NDLEA said the discovery showed how closely the cartels monitored their couriers and consignments. It added that the passport biodata page of Njambi, recovered from Henlo’s phone, was used to profile her and place her on the agency’s watchlist. She was subsequently arrested at the departure boarding gate of the Lagos airport on October 15 while attempting to board a South African Airways flight to Kenya. item.title: ‘I’ve not been served’ – Jimmy Odukoya speaks on court injunction amid church crisis
item.description: Pastor Jimmy Odukoya has said he has not been formally served with the court injunction restraining him from presenting himself as the Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head of The Fountain of Life Church, Ilupeju, Lagos. Odukoya made this known on Sunday while addressing the congregation during the church’s service, saying he had only heard about the injunction but had yet to receive the court order. “I heard that there was an injunction against me. I heard. I’ve not seen it. But I heard. But I’ve not been served. So, legally, I’ve not been served,” he said. His remarks came shortly after the founder of The Redeemed Evangelical Mission, Bishop Mike Okonkwo, made a surprise appearance at the service and urged members not to take sides in the leadership dispute involving Odukoya and his sister, Tolu. Thanking members for their continued support amid the controversy, Jimmy Odukoya said he appreciated their decision to attend the service despite the ongoing crisis. “In spite of everything, you are still here,” he told the congregation. He also reaffirmed his commitment to the church and its members, saying, “There is no Fountain without you. You are Fountain of Life. And as long as you are with me, I will continue to speak for you. I will continue to stand with you.” Describing the service as the quickest, Odukoya joked that Okonkwo had already delivered the sermon, leaving him with little to add. “Bishop has preached already. There is nothing to preach again,” he said, adding that he would finish speaking on time. He subsequently asked the congregation if they wanted another dance, to which members reportedly responded in the affirmative. Earlier, Okonkwo told the congregation that he was prompted by the Holy Spirit to visit the church and bless its members amid the leadership crisis. “I have not slept since 1.30 am. The Holy Spirit said to me, son, go to the Fountain and bless them. That’s why I am here,” he said. On Friday, Odukoya approached the Federal High Court in Lagos, challenging his reported removal as senior pastor and questioning the legality of decisions allegedly taken by some members of the church’s Board of Trustees. The suit, instituted alongside the Incorporated Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church, named his sister, Tolu Odukoya, and seven other church leaders as respondents. They include Pastors Rotimi Okpaise, Tobi Enuha, Gbenga Onabanjo, Fred Ohiani and Akin Osinbajo, as well as Biodun Balogun and Biodun Awosika. item.title: Bayelsa boat tragedy: NEMA deploys technical team as death toll rises
item.description: By Emem Idio, Yenagoa The National Emergency Management Agency ,NEMA, said it has deployed a technical team to Bayelsa State to reinforce ongoing search and rescue operations following a boat accident that has now claimed 24 lives and still counting in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area. The accident occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, at the river junction between Oweikorogha and Otuan communities. The boat was conveying passengers from Ayama to Ukubie community for a burial ceremony when it capsized. NEMA in a statement signed by Manzo Ezeki of NEMA Press Unit, said 24 survivors had been rescued, while 24 bodies had been recovered as of Saturday, bringing the number of confirmed fatalities to 24. Search and rescue operations were still ongoing at the time of the announcement. The agency disclosed that 19 of the survivors were taken to Ayama Clinic, while five others, who sustained varying degrees of injuries, were transferred to Family Care Hospital in Yenagoa for medical treatment. The deployment of the technical team followed the earlier activation of NEMA’s South-South Zonal Directorate and the mobilisation of an emergency response team from its Port Harcourt Operations Office to the accident scene. The agency said it is coordinating the rescue operation alongside the Bayelsa State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA), Nigerian Red Cross Society, Nigeria Police Force, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), local divers and other emergency responders. Governor Douye Diri visited the scene of the accident, where he expressed grief over the loss of lives and condoled with the families of the victims. He also commended the emergency agencies, security operatives, local divers and other responders for their intervention and continued efforts to locate possible survivors despite the difficult riverine terrain. NEMA expressed sympathy with the Bayelsa State Government and the families affected by the tragedy, pledging to sustain its collaboration with relevant authorities to coordinate the rescue operation. item.title: WAEC, NECO Exams: TRCN sets December deadline for teachers’ certification
item.description: ​​⁠‌‌​ The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN) has set December 2026 as deadline for schools to ensure that, at least, 75 per cent of their teachers are professionally certified and licensed. Dr. Ronke Soyombo, Registrar/Chief Executive of TRCN, disclosed this in an interview the Newsmen in Abuja on Sunday. She said the measure was aimed at strengthening compliance with professional teaching standards. Soyombo said schools would be required to meet the certification threshold to qualify to apply for the West African Examinations Council (WAEC) and National Examinations Council (NECO) examinations. ‘By December 2026, schools will be required to have at least 75 per cent of their teachers certified and licensed by TRCN to qualify to apply for WAEC and NECO examinations,’ she said. Soyombo said the council had integrated its website with WAEC and NECO through an Application Programming Interface (API) to enable the examination bodies verify teachers’ professional status. She said authorised officials of both examination bodies would be able to access the system using designated login credentials to determine schools’ compliance with the requirement. The registrar said TRCN had commenced compliance monitoring, adding that it was engaging private school owners and administrators to encourage teachers to register for professional examinations and licensing. She, however, expressed concern over the low level of compliance, noting that many teachers had passed the professional qualifying examination but failed to complete the licensing process. ‘Our position is that every practising teacher must be professionally licensed. “Teaching without the required professional credentials would no longer be tolerated,” she said Soyombo said the council was also implementing an Accelerated Teacher Professionalisation Pathway to enable teachers without professional teaching qualifications to acquire the necessary training. She disclosed that during a recent teacher recruitment exercise in Nasarawa, TRCN personnel discovered that 250 applicants had presented fake certificates out of approximately 1,000 applicants. She advised school owners to verify certificates presented by prospective employees, explaining that TRCN certificates carried QR codes that could be scanned to confirm their authenticity. The registrar added that the council was taking action against impersonation and certificate fraud, disclosing that a suspect identified as Godfrey had been remanded in prison. On improving service delivery, Soyombo said TRCN had established a six-member call centre to receive and address teachers’ complaints relating to registration, examinations and certification around the clock. She said the council had also decentralised its operations into geographical regions, with designated personnel responsible for attending to complaints and ensuring quicker responses. item.description: Members of the Fountain of Life Church have welcomed their senior pastor, Jimmy Odukoya, with cheers and chants of affection during Sunday service, days after a dispute over his leadership of the church became a subject of litigation. Please welcome to the stage Bishop Mike Okonkwo.” The welcome came amid an ongoing leadership dispute at the church, which has seen rival positions emerge over Odukoya’s status as senior pastor. On Friday, Odukoya approached the Federal High Court in Lagos, challenging his reported removal as senior pastor and questioning the legality of decisions allegedly taken by some members of the church’s Board of Trustees. The suit, instituted alongside the Incorporated Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church, named his sister, Tolu Odukoya, and seven other church leaders as respondents. They include Pastors Rotimi Okpaise, Tobi Enuha, Gbenga Onabanjo, Fred Ohiani and Akin Osinbajo, as well as Biodun Balogun and Biodun Awosika. Odukoya is challenging the validity of meetings held by some trustees on January 22, February 28 and November 16, 2026, and the decisions allegedly reached at those meetings. He is also asking the court to determine whether the trustees could remove him as senior pastor without following the procedures stipulated in the church’s constitution. The dispute became public on November 17 when a group identifying itself as members of the church’s Board of Trustees announced that Odukoya was no longer recognised as senior pastor, with immediate effect. The group reportedly cited a review of the church’s constitution and succession instructions allegedly left by the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, who died in August 2023. item.title: School building collapses, kills pupil in Abia
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA -Tragedy struck at Ehere Community Primary School, in Obingwa LGA, Abia State, last Friday, when a pupil, identified as Vincent Chiedozie Dum, was reportedly killed by a collapsed building at the school. Nine other pupils escaped death as they fled before the collapse of the building. The deceased, a primary two pupil,was said to have gone to ease himself beside the dilapidated building when the wall suddenly collapsed on him. Principal of Ehere Community Senior Secondary School, Mr. Nwogu Chioma Allen, said they have been warning the pupils and students about the dangers of going around the dilapidated buildings in the compound. Nwogu stated the deceased pupil was rescued and taken to three hospitals who rejected for medical attention. However, he said the boy was later admitted at the Abia State University Teaching Hospital, ABSUTH, Aba. He also disclosed that about 10 pupils and students were playing around the building when it suddenly collapsed and hit the victim while the pupils escaped. The Principal said; “This place contains five institutions; the Ministry of Education, Primary Schools 1 and 2 and Ehere Community Junior and Senior Secondary Schools. We have a building here that is very weak. The building over the years, has lost its strength. You know children, they have been running around and we have been chasing them , telling them not to go around the building. “Unfortunately, that afternoon, they were running around the place, up to 10 of them went , running around that building. My teachers were shouting to them, leave that area. Incidentally, the building fell on the boy, the other children were able to escape. The boy was taken to three hospitals for medical attention, but they all rejected him.” He urged the state government to extend it’s school rehabilitation projects to the Ehere Community Primary and Secondary School. “Some of the buildings here are weak. The government has been trying in the renovation of schools. We hope that our own school will be renovated to avert such situations.” When Vanguard visited the school, it was observed that the dilapidated building has been sealed off. item.title: First-Class degree not enough to make excellent teacher – TRCN
item.description: The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN) says possessing a first-class degree does not automatically make an individual an excellent teacher. Dr. Ronke Soyombo, Registrar/Chief Executive of TRCN, stated this in an interview with Newsmen on Sunday in Abuja. Soyombo stressed the importance of professional competence adding that effective teaching required more than academic qualifications. The registrar explained that teachers must demonstrate competence in five critical areas assessed through the Council’s professional qualifying examination. She identified the areas as basic mathematics, foundational literacy, digital literacy, pedagogy, and safeguarding and child protection. According to her, teachers must possess a sound understanding of basic mathematical concepts to effectively support children’s learning and development. She described foundational literacy as equally important, noting that strong literacy skills enabled teachers to support learning across other subject areas. The registrar said teachers must also understand today’s children, particularly those belonging to the Alpha Generation, and the technological environment in which they operate. She identified digital literacy as the third major area of assessment, describing it as compulsory for teachers seeking to engage effectively with contemporary learners. To illustrate the challenge, Soyombo recalled visiting an examination centre where she encountered an elderly teacher struggling with a computer mouse. “I remember visiting an examination centre recently and meeting an elderly teacher who held a computer mouse and asked me, ‘Madam, what am I going to do with this?’” she said. She said the encounter highlighted the extent of digital literacy challenges confronting some teachers and raised concerns about their preparedness for modern classrooms. “How can teachers effectively engage children in today’s classrooms if they are not comfortable with basic technology?” she asked. Soyombo, however, acknowledged the challenges and disclosed that several training programmes were being implemented to improve teachers’ digital competence. On pedagogy, she said possessing excellent academic qualifications did not automatically translate into the ability to teach effectively. “Having a first-class degree does not automatically make someone an excellent teacher,” she said. She explained that academic qualifications alone could not guarantee that a teacher understood how to apply appropriate instructional methods to address different learning needs. According to her, classrooms comprise learners with varying abilities, including average pupils, children requiring additional support, and gifted and talented learners. item.title: Full list: FG announces 19 international job vacancies [How to apply]
item.description: The Federal Government, FG has announced 19 international job vacancies for qualified Nigerians at the African Space Agency and the General Secretariat of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC). The vacancies, announced by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, comprise five positions at the African Space Agency headquarters in Cairo, Egypt, and 14 positions at the OIC headquarters in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. The ministry disclosed this in two separate vacancy announcements dated Friday, November 20, 2026, signed by its spokesperson, Oluwafemi Adeniyi, and shared on its official Facebook page on Saturday. According to the ministry, the African Space Agency is recruiting for five positions, with application deadlines of November 25 and December 10, 2026. The positions include Director, Corporate Services (D-1); Director-General, African Space Agency (D-2); Head of Legal Affairs (Grade P-5); Senior Finance Officer (P3); and Senior Human Resources Officer (P3). The ministry said interested and qualified Nigerians should visit the agency’s official website at https://africanspaceagency.org for details of the eligibility requirements and application procedures. For the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, the ministry announced 14 vacancies across its departments and specialised units. The positions include Director-General of Political Affairs; Director, Administration Department; Director, Information Department; Director, Conference Department; Director, Muslim Communities and Minorities; Director, African Affairs; and Director, European Affairs and International Organisations. Others are Head of Human Resources (PP2); Professional Officer, Human Resources (PP2); Professional Officers, Administration Department (P2); Director, Peace, Security and Mediation Unit; Chief of HRC Office – IUT; Registrar – IUT; and Deputy Internal Auditor – IUT. The ministry said the application deadlines for the OIC positions range from November 29 to December 24, 2026. It urged interested and qualified Nigerians to visit the organisation’s official vacancy portal at https://www.oic-oci.org/en/vacancies for information on the specific requirements, application procedures and deadlines for each position. How to apply Interested Nigerians can apply through the following official platforms: African Space Agency: Visit https://africanspaceagency.org , navigate to the recruitment or careers section, and check the available positions, eligibility criteria and application instructions. Organisation of Islamic Cooperation: Visit https://www.oic-oci.org/en/vacancies , select the relevant vacancy and follow the stated application procedure. Applicants are advised to review the requirements for their preferred positions and submit their applications before the respective deadlines. item.title: Dickson mourns victims of Bayelsa boat mishap, seeks safety measures
item.description: Former Governor of Bayelsa State, Senator Henry Seriake Dickson, has commiserated with the families and friends of victims of the boat mishap along the Ayama/Oweikorogha waterways in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of the state. Dickson, who disclosed this in a post on his X platform on Sunday, described the incident as unfortunate and expressed sadness over the loss of lives. He also extended his condolences to the Bayelsa State Government and the people of the state over the tragedy. The senator said he deliberately scaled down his engagements on Saturday as a mark of respect for those who lost their lives in the incident. According to him, he reduced the number of visitors he attended to and cancelled some previously scheduled visits to reflect on the tragedy. Dickson commended the relevant emergency response agencies and other individuals involved in the rescue operation for their swift response, urging them to sustain their efforts until the operation was successfully concluded. He also called for stricter enforcement of maritime safety regulations and increased public awareness to prevent similar incidents. The former governor stressed the need for continuous safety education for marine operators, security personnel and residents of Bayelsa State. He further urged traditional institutions and the media to support efforts aimed at promoting maritime safety and ensuring compliance with relevant regulations. Dickson reiterated his condolences to the bereaved families, praying that God would grant the deceased eternal rest and give their loved ones the strength to bear the loss. item.description: A survivor of Friday’s boat accident in the Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has recounted how she struggled to escape from the capsized vessel, saying she lost several members of her family and neighbours in the tragedy. The woman, whose identity was not immediately disclosed, said her elder sister, her sister’s daughter-in-law and two children belonging to her relatives and neighbours were among those who died in the accident. Recounting the incident, she said the boat suddenly capsized, trapping passengers beneath it. “The boat just fell and pressed all of us. My elder sister’s son’s wife was lost. My elder sister was lost. Her son was also lost. One of my neighbours who followed us also lost her son. My neighbour herself was lost,” she said. ﻿ The survivor said she was the only person among those close to her who made it out alive, adding that she struggled to escape after the boat overturned. “It’s only me that is safe. When I came out, somebody held me. I was drinking water. I was not able to come out. I struggled before I came out. Where we were standing, the boat broke from above and pressed us down,” she said. Asked by the Bayelsa governor, Douye Diri, whether the bodies of her missing relatives and neighbours had been recovered, she replied in the negative. Her account comes as the death toll from the accident has risen to 23, while 24 survivors are receiving treatment in hospitals. However, a survivor had also alleged that the wooden passenger vessel, popularly known as a ‘love boat’, was overloaded with passengers and their belongings, raising concerns about possible breaches of waterway safety regulations. President Bola Tinubu has expressed condolences to the families of the victims and directed relevant federal disaster response agencies to support rescue and recovery operations. item.title: Can Enzo Maresca Win The Premier League In His First Season At Man City?
item.description: Six league titles. Ten years. A stand at the Etihad with his name on it. Good luck following that. Enzo Maresca has to, after Manchester City unveiled him as manager back in June 2026. Maresca at least knows his way around the training ground. Back in 2020-2021, he ran the Elite Development Squad and won Premier League 2 with them. He returned in 2022 to work under Guardiola as an assistant, and that season ended with the treble. So this is spell number three, and he’s tied down until 2029. Expectations at City don’t reset just because the man in the dugout has changed. City’s title odds have become some of the most debated in premier league online betting markets because bookmakers must weigh a campaign shaped as much by events off the pitch as on it. A Flying Start, Then A Bump The opening weeks went better than almost anyone expected. Maresca became the first manager in Premier League history to win his first seven games in charge of a new club. The football looked familiar too. City kept the ball and wore teams down, which is no surprise from a coach who learned so much from Guardiola. His Leicester and Chelsea sides played the same way. City spent big to help him. Their summer outlay of around £460 million was a record for any club, and £125 million of it went on Enzo Fernández from Chelsea, a fee that matched the Premier League transfer record. Phil Foden signed a four-year extension. Rodri, one of the faces of the Guardiola years, left for Barcelona. Maresca has won quickly before. He lifted the Championship title with Leicester in 2023-24. A year later at Chelsea, he won the Conference League and the Club World Cup and still finished fourth in the league. Seven straight wins at the start of a season guarantee nothing, of course. Plenty of fast starters have slid down the Premier League table once the winter fixtures arrive. City soon lost three league games in a row, one of them a 1-0 home defeat to Brighton, who had never won away at City before. Then there are Arsenal. Mikel Arteta, another former Guardiola assistant, ended their 22-year wait for the title in 2025-26, helped along by a Premier League record for goals from corners. item.title: Death Toll In Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 23
item.description: The death toll from Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 23, with 24 survivors receiving treatment in hospitals. The accident occurred when a boat conveying mourners to a burial ceremony capsized near Oweikorogha Community in the Ukubie area of Southern Ijaw. The Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed the incident in a statement, saying the boat was travelling from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony on Friday, when it capsized at about 11 a.m. A preliminary police report indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways. Following the incident, rescue operations were launched, with several passengers rescued while others were initially reported missing. A survivor had also alleged that the wooden passenger boat, popularly known as a ‘love boat’, was overloaded with passengers and their belongings, suggesting that this might have contributed to the accident. President Bola Tinubu has expressed condolences to the families of the victims, describing the incident as tragic and directing relevant federal disaster response agencies to support rescue and recovery efforts. In a statement posted on his X account, Tinubu said, “Those who lost their lives in the tragedy did not deserve to die that way. I have directed all relevant Federal Disaster Response agencies to work together to ensure a successful recovery and rescue operation.” The President also directed that the presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, on Saturday, be held without much fanfare in honour of those who lost their lives. “On behalf of the entire nation, I mourn those who lost their lives in the incident and sympathise with their families, the government and the people of Bayelsa State. “I particularly mourn with Governor Douye Diri over this sad incident. I pray that God Almighty repose their souls and comfort their families,” he said. Meanwhile, Governor Douye Diri has visited the scene of the accident and is expected to initiate a probe into the circumstances surrounding the tragedy. The state government has also warned boat operators against overloading, reckless navigation and travelling without life jackets, stressing the need for strict compliance with waterway safety regulations. item.title: China Diaries: The Railway Connecting Continents
item.description: Standing at the Xi’an International Port Station in northwest China, watching the movement of freight trains preparing to transport goods across borders and continents, I was reminded that economic development is not only about what a country produces. It is also about how efficiently it can move what it produces to the rest of the world. Xi’an occupies an interesting place in China’s history. It was once the starting point of the ancient Silk Road, which connected China to Central Asia, the Middle East and Europe through centuries of trade and cultural exchange. Today, the city is reclaiming that historic role through a modern railway network that connects Chinese manufacturing centres to markets across Europe and Asia. The China-Europe Railway Express is one of the most visible outcomes of China’s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). Through this network, freight trains transport automobiles, electronics, machinery, textiles, agricultural products and other goods across the Eurasian continent. What makes the initiative particularly interesting is how it has transformed the economic possibilities of a city located thousands of kilometres from the sea. Xi’an has become an important international logistics hub, demonstrating that geographical distance from a coastline does not have to limit a city’s participation in global trade. The railway network has continued to expand. By November 2025, China-Europe freight trains had completed nearly 120,000 journeys, connecting 232 cities in 26 European countries and more than 100 cities in 11 Asian countries. The value of goods transported through the network had reached $426.4 billion by the end of 2024. These are not merely impressive transportation figures. They represent an evolving system of economic connectivity, linking manufacturers, suppliers, distributors and consumers across national borders. Beyond transportation: The economics of connectivity The significance of the railway goes beyond moving containers from one destination to another. It creates opportunities for businesses to reach markets faster, diversify their supply chains and reduce their dependence on a single transportation route. Rail freight offers an important middle ground between air and sea transportation. While it is generally more expensive than shipping by sea, it can be considerably faster. For certain categories of goods, particularly machinery, automobile components, electronics and other time-sensitive products, that difference can be commercially significant. It also provides an alternative when disruptions affect other transportation routes. Another important feature is the development of inland logistics infrastructure. Warehousing, customs processing, container handling, industrial parks and distribution services have grown around railway connections.
